excerpts.translation:
TAG
—572—
TAG
house, when many people climb onto it. Nata-
gostos, 1, nag, to creak, or make such a sound with the bindings,
and an insect that damages the palay.
TAGOTOGNAN. pe. A wild fruit, like tomatoes, and it is edible, and the leaf, like eggplant.
TAGPE. pe. A blow, that is given with the broad side of
the knife. Napatatagpé, to strike with the broad side of the knife, or sword, as with the back, or flat side.
Pinatatagpean, to be struck with the back or flat side, Ypi-
natatagpé, the sword, or knife, with which it is struck,
time, and cause.
TAGPO. pe. A tree so named, that yields a
small edible fruit: the same is, Alitatpó.
TAGPOC. pe. Imperat. Natagpoc, 1, nag, to stab, with some knife, balarao, or dagger.
